body.hook: Spanish is the official language of 20 countries and spoken by over 480 million native speakers, from Madrid to Mexico City, from Bogotá to Buenos Aires. Each region has its own foods, music, accents and traditions.

study.title: El mundo hispanohablante
study.question: Where is Spanish spoken, and how do cultures differ?
study.passage:
Regions and countries:
• Europe: España (Spain).
• North and Central America: México, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica, Panamá.
• Caribbean: Cuba, República Dominicana, Puerto Rico (US territory).
• South America: Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, Perú, Bolivia, Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay.
• Africa: Guinea Ecuatorial.
Diversity: Many Indigenous languages are spoken alongside Spanish: Quechua (Peru, Bolivia), Guaraní (Paraguay, official alongside Spanish), Maya languages (Guatemala, Mexico), Náhuatl (Mexico).
Cultural features (examples): Mexico: Día de Muertos (November 1–2), mariachi, tacos. Spain: flamenco, tapas, late dinners around 9 or 10 p.m. Argentina: tango, mate, asado. Peru: Machu Picchu, ceviche. Colombia: cumbia, vallenato, arepas.
Texto:
Me llamo Mateo y vivo en Cusco, Perú. Hablo español y quechua. Cusco está en los Andes, a 3,400 metros de altura. Aquí hace más frío que en Lima. Mi comida favorita es el ceviche, pero en Cusco comemos mucha sopa porque es una ciudad fría.
Task: Label 21 countries on a map. Research one country and compare it with Canada using three comparisons.
